title: Instrumental 4: Professions and Identities
description: Professions take instrumental after работать, быть (past / future), and стать. Я работаю инженером.
descriptionRussian: Названия профессий ставятся в творительном падеже после работать, быть и стать.
intro: Saying what someone does for a living puts the job in this case, which is a small surprise: a job is not a tool and not company. Think of it as the role you act through. There is a catch worth knowing now. In the present tense Russian has no verb 'to be', so a job named in the present stays in its plain dictionary form and only shifts once a tense appears.
rules: After работать (to work), the profession goes in the instrumental: работать кем. Я работаю инженером (I work as an engineer).
After быть in the past (был / была / было / были) or future (буду / будешь / будет / будем / будете / будут), the profession goes in the instrumental: Антон будет учителем.
After стать (to become; perfective), the result-state goes in the instrumental: Лена стала врачом.
In the present tense, быть has no overt form, and the predicate noun stays NOMINATIVE: 'Антон — учитель' (Anton is a teacher). The instrumental only applies with the three verbs above.
Russian normally uses the masculine profession form for both male and female subjects: Маша работает врачом, not врачихой.
examples: Я работаю инженером. (I work as an engineer.) инженер → инженером.
Маша работает врачом. (Masha works as a doctor.) врач → врачом.
Антон будет учителем. (Anton will be a teacher.) учитель → учителем.
Лена стала программистом. (Lena became a programmer.) программист → программистом.
Соня будет переводчиком. (Sonya will be a translator.) переводчик → переводчиком.

items.hint: Recall L3: с + which case? Лена is feminine -а.
items.explanation: Warm-up from Lesson 3. С takes the instrumental: Лена → Леной. Today we move to a different instrumental construction (work / be / become as), but the form of the noun is calculated the same way.

items.hint: Работать + the profession takes the instrumental.
items.explanation: After работать (to work), the profession goes in the instrumental: работать кем → врачом. Russian uses the masculine form even when Masha is female; this is the standard convention.

items.hint: Same construction as Q1.2. Apply the masculine hard rule.
items.explanation: Инженер is masculine consonant + -ом → инженером. Note that работать + instrumental applies only to professions and roles, not to tools (tools take с or bare instrumental, never работать).

items.hint: Будет (future of быть) takes the same case as работать for professions.
items.explanation: Future-tense быть (буду, будешь, будет...) plus a profession takes the instrumental: будет переводчиком. The same is true of past-tense был / была: был переводчиком.

items.hint: Стать takes which case for the result-state?
items.explanation: Стать (to become; perfective) takes the result-state in the instrumental: стать кем → программистом. Стать pairs with становиться (imperfective) which works the same way.

items.hint: Учитель is masculine soft -ь. Apply the L1 soft rule.
items.explanation: Учитель is masculine ending in soft -ь with stem stress → -ем: учителем. Modern Russian uses the masculine form for female subjects in most professions; this is the safe default at A2.

items.promptEnglish: Masha works as a salesclerk in a shop.
items.explanation: After работать the profession goes in the instrumental: работает продавцом.

items.promptEnglish: After college Anton became an artist.
items.hint: Стать takes the result-state in which case?
items.explanation: Стать ('to become') takes the instrumental: стал художником. The new role always stands in the instrumental.

items.promptEnglish: Lena will be a bus driver.
items.hint: Быть in the future takes the profession in which case?
items.explanation: The future of быть takes the instrumental for a role: будет водителем. Soft-stem masculines take -ем: водителем.

blanks: Маша будет _____. (Masha will be a writer.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Писатель is masculine ending in soft -ь with stem stress → -ем: писателем. The construction 'будет + instrumental' marks the future profession or role.

errorCorrection.sentence: Моя сестра работает повар в кафе.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: My sister works as a cook at a cafe.
errorCorrection.explanation: After работать, the profession goes in the instrumental: работать кем. Повар is hard masculine + -ом: поваром. Повар is the bare nominative, correct only in a verbless identity ('Моя сестра - повар').

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: After university Anton became a journalist.
errorCorrection.explanation: Стать (to become) takes the result-state in the instrumental: стать кем. Журналист is hard masculine + -ом: журналистом. Журналист is the bare nominative, used only in a verbless identity ('Антон - журналист').

errorCorrection.sentence: Мой папа учителем в нашей школе.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: My dad is a teacher at our school.
errorCorrection.explanation: In the present tense, быть has no spoken form and the predicate noun stays NOMINATIVE: 'Мой папа учитель'. The instrumental учителем appears only with an actual verb: работает учителем, был учителем, станет учителем. Here there is no verb, so the form is the nominative учитель.

minimalPairs.explanation: After работать the profession goes in the instrumental: врачом. The nominative врач would only mark a subject ('Врач здесь.' / 'The doctor is here.'), or the predicate of a present-tense identity ('Маша — врач.' / 'Masha is a doctor.').
Same pattern: работать + instrumental → инженером. The choice between nominative and instrumental for professions is determined entirely by the verb in play (or its absence in present-tense быть).

reviewVocab.definition: profession (in Russian, profession-as-instrumental appears with работать, быть past / future, and стать)
to become (perfective; takes the result-state in the instrumental: стать кем)
to work (the 'works as X' construction takes the instrumental: работать кем)
